members.name: Sugarloaf Point Lighthouse
members.bio: 1875 lighthouse above Seal Rocks, one of two Australian towers with an external stairway.

members.name: Seal Rocks
members.bio: Remote fishing village in Myall Lakes National Park with five beaches, a blowhole and good surf.

members.name: Number One Beach
members.bio: First beach into Seal Rocks, sheltered for swimming, with small learner waves and a point break at its end.

members.name: Treachery Headland Walking Track
members.bio: A 2 km return walk through coastal rainforest to a grassy headland with views of Sugarloaf Point Lighthouse.
members.photo_file: Treachery Beach And Headland NSW Australia.jpg

members.name: Yacaaba Headland Walking Track
members.bio: Steep 7 km return climb above Hawks Nest to headland views of Port Stephens, Seal Rocks and the coast.

members.name: Dark Point Walking Track
members.bio: A 2 km return walk behind the dunes to Dark Point, a Worimi gathering place for at least 4,000 years.

members.name: Big Oyster
members.bio: A roadside giant oyster, once a restaurant and shop, now the upper floor of a Taree car dealership.
members.hours: Visible from the road at any time

members.name: Crowdy Bay National Park
members.bio: Coastal park between Port Macquarie and Taree with beach camping, headland lookouts and dune walks.

members.name: Old Bar
members.bio: Surf village near Taree with a summer-patrolled beach, kite-boarding and a 2.5 km path to Wallabi Point.
members.photo_file: The Old Bar Beach - Taken on the Saturday, 7th January 2012 at 11-53am. - panoramio.jpg

members.name: Big Axe
members.bio: Giant roadside axe at Kew, first built in 1979 for a local axeman and the timber trade, rebuilt in 2017.

members.name: Urunga
members.bio: Town where the Bellinger and Kalang rivers reach the sea, beside Hungry Head Beach to the south.

members.name: Hungry Head Beach
members.bio: Largely untouched beach south of Urunga, with lifeguards at the car-accessible southern end.

members.name: Captain Cook Lookout
members.bio: Clifftop lookout at the end of Parkes Street over the Nambucca River mouth, good for whales and dolphins.

members.name: Antarctic Beech Forest Walking Track
members.bio: A 2.5 km loop through snow gum woodland and Antarctic beech rainforest, with mossy cascades and a gorge.

members.name: Careys Peak Lookout
members.bio: A 14 km return track along the escarpment to a lookout over the Barrington wilderness and Hunter Valley.
